Notwithstanding
not-with-STAND-ing
conjunction
A literal English rendering of the Latin ablative absolute non obstante, “not standing in the way”; hence “although this stands against it,” “nevertheless” — the obstacle is granted, and then overruled.

Biblical Definition

Notwithstanding is the Authorized Version’s great word of overruling. It does not deny the obstacle; it grants it and then walks past it. Its native strength appears in Php 1:18, where Paul, bound in prison and preached against by men of envy and strife: “What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.” The bad motives are real and are not excused — and they do not stand in the way of the gospel’s spread nor of the apostle’s joy. That is the whole doctrine of providence compressed into one connective: God’s purpose is not contingent upon the goodness of the instruments. The same word puts joy in its right order when the seventy return elated: “Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven” (Luk 10:20). Power over devils is granted — and overruled by election. At the end, deserted at his first answer, Paul writes, “Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me” (2Ti 4:17). All men forsook him; the obstacle is granted; the Lord stood. So also 1Ti 2:15 turns the sentence upon Eve toward hope. Wherever the AV says notwithstanding, a Christian may look for the sovereign hand that lets the difficulty be exactly what it is and accomplishes His will through it anyway.

Webster 1828 Definition

Nevertheless; however; without hindrance from — the obstacle granted and then overruled.

expand to see more

NOTWITHSTANDING, without hindrance or obstruction from; nevertheless; however.

Literally not withstanding — the thing named does not stand in the way.

An English calque of the Latin non obstante, a formula of legal overruling.

It concedes the obstacle honestly, then declares it insufficient.

Paul: notwithstanding, every way Christ is preached, and I therein do rejoice (Php 1:18).

Key Scripture

Php 1:18 — "What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice."

Luk 10:20 — "Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven."

2Ti 4:17 — "Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion."

1Ti 2:15 — "Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety."

Modern Corruption

The word survives; what has been lost is the doctrine it carries — that God overrules real obstacles without pretending they are not there.

expand to see more

The modern corruption is not of the word but of the comfort it carries, and it comes in two forms. The first is the denial of the obstacle: a cheerful religion that tells the afflicted their trouble is not really trouble, that the envy is not really envy, that the loss is not really loss. Scripture never does this. Paul names the pretence as pretence and the strife as strife, and only then says notwithstanding. Honest naming is the precondition of real comfort. The second form is the denial of the overruling: the practical unbelief that grants the obstacle full weight and stops there, as though the church’s enemies, the preacher’s bad motives, or the saint’s own weakness could halt the purpose of God. Both errors flee the sentence Paul actually wrote, which holds the wound and the victory in a single breath.

The principle to recover is providence in its confessional strength: God ordains whatsoever comes to pass, and He works even through the crooked instruments of envious men without being the author of their sin. The gospel preached out of contention is still the gospel; the sermon of a man whose heart is wrong still carries a word that is right, and the Spirit still saves by it. That is not indifference to the preacher’s heart — Paul elsewhere warns such men severely — but it is a wall against despair for saints who look at the state of the church and conclude the cause is lost. It never is. All men forsook Paul; notwithstanding, the Lord stood with him. Devils submitted to the seventy; notwithstanding, their names in heaven were the better joy. Learn the word, and learn to say it in the dark.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means “this does not stand in the way” — nevertheless.

expand to see more

Notwithstanding — literally not withstanding, not standing against.

An English calque of Latin non obstante, the lawyer’s clause of overruling.

It grants the obstacle honestly, then declares it powerless to stop the end.

Php 1:18 makes it the hinge of providence: Christ is preached either way.

2Ti 4:17: all forsook Paul — notwithstanding, the Lord stood with him.

Usage

"Notwithstanding never denies the difficulty; it grants it and overrules it."

"Christ is preached of envy and of good will — notwithstanding, Christ is preached."

"Rejoice not that devils submit; notwithstanding, rejoice that your name is written in heaven."
